bull_bear.body: Prioritizing capex for capacity expansion (80%+); dividend recommended at 125% of face value (Rs.12.5/share); no buybacks mentioned; JV funding for export unit to be equity-funded
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Labor migration volatility (seasonal/election-linked); steel price spikes (managed but not eliminated); execution risk in new heavy structure segment; JV partner dependency for export market access; regulatory delays in project clearances
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Highly confident, proactive, and execution-focused; emphasized preparedness over opportunism; clear roadmap for capacity and segment expansion; dismissed margin pressure concerns with pricing discipline; tone suggests market leadership ambition
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Rs.102cr order for Rajpath government building signals entry into high-profile public infrastructure; JV for North American joists is a strategic pivot to capture export demand with zero domestic competition; labor disruption in March was election-linked, not structural; heavy structure plant enables entry into stadiums, airports, and high-rises — a $50bn+ TAM beyond traditional PEB
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- "Debt-free company with high cash reserves and strong financial performance" is stated as a key strength and repeated as "A debt-free company with a high cash reserve demonstrating strong financial stability and growth potential."
- Net Debt (INR Cr.) is shown negative across the period: -41 (FY23), -48 (FY24), -182 (FY25), -66 (FY26); the FY26 balance sheet shows non-current borrowings of 0.0 and current borrowings of 15.0.
- Returns as printed: RoCE 26.80% / 25.80% / 18.83% / 21.26% and RoE 20.40% / 19.40% / 14.35% / 15.27% for FY23 / FY24 / FY25 / FY26.
- Cash conversion turned negative in FY26: "Net Cash from Operating Activities" of -18.8 (vs 53.6 in FY25, 81.5 in FY24), driven by "Changes in working capital" of -164.6, with trade receivables (current) rising to 288.2 and non-current trade receivables to 111.0.
- The MD commits to "disciplined execution, prudent capital allocation and continuous operational improvement"; the deck states no dividend, payout or buyback policy anywhere.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: Industrial: 87% of FY26 revenue (up from 77%); Non-industrial: 13% (data centers, high-rise, government buildings); Heavy structure: currently <10% of revenue but growing fast with new plant; Export: Rs.40cr in FY26 (Africa, Canada, Myanmar); New wins: CESC Green Power, Lodha Logistics, Hero Scooters (L&T), Rajpath government building (Rs.102cr)
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- "Ranked among integrated PEB players in India in FY25: 2nd", with "Market share among integrated PEB players in India: 6.5%" and "Presence in the PEB and Building Products Industry: 40+ Years".
- Six listed key strengths: integrated manufacturing backed by in-house design/engineering and on-site project management; market position and brand presence; execution track record; diverse customer base with long-standing relationships; experienced promoters and management; and "Debt-free company with high cash reserves and strong financial performance."
- Scale of delivery: "850+ Completed execution of PEB Contracts from FY15 to FY26", with projects cited across an airport (Delhi), a data centre (Navi Mumbai), solar PV module plants (Dholera and Jaipur), hospitals, food processing and industrial & logistics parks.
- Industry structure favours the company's cohort: organised players are 40-45% of the Indian PEB market with top 6 players at 80-85% of the organised segment, and FY19-23 CAGR of 11.4% for Top 6 Players vs 8.5% Total Industry and 7.0% Rest of the Industry (Source: Prospectus).
- Customer stickiness: "3 of 5 Customer Groups have been associated for over five years" and repeat orders were 72% of revenue from operations in FY26 (80% FY23, 81% FY24, 82% FY25).
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Order book] "Total Order book as on 31st July 2026, is INR 1,864 Cr", with "Order Wins (Rs in Crs) 609" for "Orders booked between 01st May 2026 and 31st July 2026" and a "major order worth Rs. 165 crore in Gujarat" secured during the quarter. The order-book pie prints 30% and 70% against an "Industrial / Infrastructure" legend, but the label-to-value binding is not recoverable from the extract, so the split is not asserted here.
- [JV] Joint Venture Agreement with ER Steel Inc, Canada — Interarch 76% / ER Steel 24% — "to establish a structured framework for jointly evaluating the design, engineering, manufacturing and supply of OWSJ products through a scalable and cost-efficient platform in India". Interarch leads engineering, detailing, manufacturing and quality compliance from India; ER Steel supports market development and sales in USA & Canada.
- [JV terms] "Total funding required by the JV company to procure land, to undertake the development and operationalization of the Business is expected to be INR 80 Crs", and "ER Steel must enter into 100% Offtake Agreement with the JV Co and purchase the total quantity of OWSJ products for distribution and sale in Canada & USA. This is a major commercial assurance for the JV."
- [Export tie-up] Collaboration with Mold-Tek Technologies Limited (MTTL): Interarch handles manufacturing and logistics while MTTL provides detailing for PEB and structural steel projects; a "two-year business plan, extendable by mutual consent", exclusivity "on projects introduced by MTTL", and Interarch pays MTTL "a commission on export orders generated through MTTL's efforts".
- [Export certifications] "Certificate for Inspection Program for Manufacturer of Metal Building System issued by IAS used to supply the pre-engineered buildings in USA" and an "International Code Council – Certificate issued to supply LGFS products in the USA".
- [Name change / one-off] The company is "Formerly known as Interarch Building Products Limited"; FY26 carries an Exceptional Item of -3.2 footnoted as a "One time statutory impact of new Labour Codes".
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: EBITDA margin held at 9.3% despite Rs.5.5cr one-off costs (export certifications, labor code compliance, outsourced high-rise engineering); steel price volatility managed via dynamic bidding; no margin erosion despite Q4 steel price rise due to forward pricing discipline
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: revenue growth: Rs.2,150-2,200cr for FY27 (15%+ YoY); margin: stable at ~9-10% despite new segment costs; order inflow: robust pipeline (Rs.800-900cr P1, Rs.3,500cr P2); capex/commissioning: Gujarat PEB Phase-1 (July 2026), Andhra Heavy Structure Phase-1 (July 2026), Phase-2/3 of heavy structure by FY28, total capacity to reach 60,000 tons by Dec 2027
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Rs.1,700cr as of end-Q4FY26; includes Rs.102cr new order announced post-quarter (to recognize in Q1FY27); backlog covers next 9 months at Rs.550-600cr/quarter
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Heavy structure capacity (Andhra) unlocking non-industrial bids; 100% export JV in India for North American open web joists (MoU signed, plant by Aug/Sep 2027); expansion of Gujarat plant to 60,000 tons by Dec 2027; potential entry into solar rooftops and modular hospitals
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Interarch delivered 31% YoY revenue growth despite Q4 volume flattening due to prior capacity utilization, with order book surging to Rs.1,700cr and heavy structure capacity ramping up to capture non-industrial demand; margin resilience despite Rs.5.5cr one-off costs and export certifications signals strong pricing power and execution discipline.

open.item: Total installed capacity (PEB + HSS) is expected to reach 2,65,000 MT by Q3 FY 2026-27.
Gujarat manufacturing facility Phase II is expected to be completed before December 2026.
Heavy Steel Structures capacity is set to reach 60,000 MT by 2027.
The dedicated Athivaram Heavy Steel Structures (HSS) facility is being commissioned in August 2026 and is expected to be commercialised by FY 2026-27.
Management has an aspiration to achieve export orders of INR 100 crore in FY 2026-27, building on FY26 export orders of INR 40.2 crore.

Following a Members' approval of variation of IPO-proceeds objects (postal ballot, March 27, 2026), the revised object — development of Andhra Pradesh Manufacturing Facility II funded from reallocated unutilised IPO proceeds — is proposed to be completed on or before March 31, 2027.
Land has already been acquired for a sixth, fully integrated manufacturing plant in Gujarat, which should begin production by FY 2027-28.
The QIP-funded capex plan is expected to double heavy steel structure capacity and support a targeted revenue milestone of INR 2,500 crore by FY 2027-28.
Land has already been acquired for a sixth manufacturing plant in Gujarat, which should begin production by FY 2027-28.

The Company expects to increase its overall installed manufacturing capacity to nearly 2,65,000 metric tonnes per annum, aided by the Kheda (Gujarat) facility and the new Heavy Steel Structures plant.
Management's near-term focus is on taking manufacturing capacity past 2,00,000 MT.
The Company initiated a INR 100 crore Qualified Institutional Placement (QIP) for capital expenditure, planned to double heavy steel structure capacity.
The Company has sufficient land and plans in place for a future Phase III expansion of the Andhra Pradesh HSS facility as demand continues to grow.

The Company intends to set up a dedicated 50:50 joint venture in India to manufacture Open Web Steel Joists (OWSJ) solely for export, following a strategic understanding with ER Steel INC. to grow its presence in Canada and the wider North American structural-steel market.
Phase II of the Andhra Pradesh HSS project has already commenced and is expected to become operational during the first half of 2027.
The Company is expanding captive rooftop solar capacity beyond the 1 MW already installed at Kichha and Pantnagar, with similar projects at Chennai and Andhra Pradesh well advanced.

The Company is scaling its global footprint through landmark export collaborations in North America while working on advanced manufacturing facilities, complex multi-storey institutional buildings and critical transport infrastructure.

The Company is building a dedicated Heavy Steel Structures (HSS) plant on a 20-acre site next to its Andhra Pradesh facility, funded via a strategic QIP fundraise of INR 100 crore, expected to enhance heavy-structures capabilities.
The Company is developing a new PEB manufacturing facility at Kheda, Gujarat, to build a stronger pan-India manufacturing presence and serve West/Central India industrial corridors.
The Company has contracted capital commitments of INR 6,925.82 Lacs remaining to be executed (net of advances) as at 31 March 2026, up from INR 3,016.36 Lacs a year earlier.

drhp.business: Interarch manufactures, supplies, erects and installs pre-engineered building (PEB) systems and related metal products, running the full project life-cycle in-house from estimation, detailed engineering and structural design through fabrication, on-site installation and erection. It serves Indian conglomerates, multinational corporations and public sector entities across industrial, manufacturing, infrastructure, commercial and residential building projects, and during FY26 entered the high-rise building segment with structural steel solutions for two NCR projects.

drhp.expansion: During FY26 Interarch commissioned Phase II of its Athivaram (Andhra Pradesh) PEB facility and a third production line at Kichha (both operational since September 2025), plus a new automated box column line in Uttarakhand, taking total PEB capacity to 2,01,000 MTPA. The Company also commenced construction of two strategically important projects: a new PEB manufacturing facility in Gujarat (its first production base in Western India, targeting the Gujarat/Maharashtra markets) and a Heavy Steel Structures (HSS) manufacturing facility in Andhra Pradesh.
